article.articleHeadline: Fumacê contra a dengue passa por cinco regiões de Campo Grande
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue Fogging Passes Through Five Regions of Campo Grande.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fogging is underway in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, as municipal health authorities intensify vector control. On Friday, 27 November 2026, five city regions — Aero Rancho, Bandeirantes, Jacy, Lageado, and Taquarussu — will receive ultra-low-volume fumigation to kill adult Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, the primary transmitters of dengue, Zika, and Chikungunya. Operations, run by the Coordenadoria de Controle de Endemias Vetoriais (CCEV) under the Municipal Health Secretariat (Sesau), run from 4:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Vehicle itineraries and the fumacê application target adult female mosquitoes. Residents are advised to keep doors and windows open during fumacê passes to improve indoor penetration. Weather conditions may cause delays or cancellations due to rain, strong winds, or fog; ad hoc adjustments will be made.

triage.headline_ja: カンポ・グランデの5地域でデング熱対策の燻蒸(フマセ)実施

article.articleHeadline: Casos de dengue aumentaram 34 vezes no mundo em 34 anos. O que explica esse avanço?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue cases have increased 34-fold worldwide over 34 years. What explains this rise?
article.articleSummary: Worldwide dengue cases rose 34-fold from 430,000 in 1990 to 14.7 million in 2024, driven by rapid urbanization and warming that expand Aedes aegypti transmission, according to ASTMH and Nature. In Brazil, about 32 million Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti were released between January 2021 and May 2022; a cohort of roughly 6,000 children was followed through 2024 with annual blood sampling to assess infections, showing a 68% lower dengue infection probability in areas with releases. Limitations include incomplete replacement of the mosquito population and potential reductions in herd immunity, underscoring the need to pair releases with dengue vaccination. Separately, environmental repellent devices produced mixed results: a Peru 2016–2019 trial reported a 34% reduction in dengue infections, while Puerto Rico 2024–2025 installations (over 50,000 devices) showed no significant effect, highlighting regional variability and the need for further testing.

triage.headline_ja: 世界のデング熱症例は34年間で34倍に増加。この急増の要因は？
triage.triage_reason: 特定国での急性アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、世界的なデング熱増加傾向とウォルバキア蚊リリース・忌避装置の効果に関する科学的レビュー記事であり、緊急対応を要するシグナルではない。
triage.notes: 記事は世界規模のデング熱増加トレンドとWolbachia蚊リリース・環境忌避装置の効果に関する研究紹介記事。ブラジルでの具体的な介入研究（Wolbachia蚊リリース、約6000人の小児コホート）が述べられているためBrazilのみverified_locationsに含めた。Peru・Puerto Rico・United Statesは対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Za a fara gwajin sabuwar allurar rigakafin cutar Ebola a Afirka
article.articleSummary: WHO ta ayyana barkewar Ebola a Jamhuriyar Dimukuradiyyar Kwango (DRC) a watan Mayu 2026, tare da mutuwa fiye da 5,700 da kama sama da 11,000. Kwararrun kiwon lafiya sun soma gwajin sabuwar allurar rigakafin Ebola a Uganda a wannan Juma’a, yayin da a ranar Litinin za a fara amfani da allurar a DRC, musamman ga mutanen Gabashin kasar, inda nau’in cutar Bundibugyo ya fi kamari. A wannan shekara ta Mayu 2026, WHO ta kara tabbatar da barkewar annoba a duniya, tare da hasashen kara daukar matakan rigakafi don dakile yaduwar cutar.

article.articleHeadline: Ugandoje pradėti mRNR vakcinos nuo Ebolos tyrimai
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Uganda to begin Ebola mRNA vaccine trials.
article.articleSummary: Two experimental Ebola vaccines are to be tested in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), at the epicenter of the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak, with trials prioritizing contacts and other high-risk individuals. The World Health Organization notes there are currently no vaccines or approved therapies for Bundibugyo virus. Since May, the DRC outbreak has surpassed 11,000 cases and about 5,700 deaths. Meanwhile, Uganda’s Virology Institute, in collaboration with Moderna, launched Africa’s first Phase I trial of one of the vaccines, using mRNA technology; the study will enroll 224 healthy volunteers aged 1–65 to assess safety and immunogenicity. Despite a long, porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has previously contained Ebola spread; earlier this year there were imported cases, and in August Uganda was declared to have halted transmission, reporting 20 infections and 2 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: السيدا ترتفع بـ78 % في منطقة "مينا"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: AIDS cases rise by 78% in the Mina area.
article.articleSummary: UN AIDS reports rising AIDS cases, with Mina region recording lowest knowledge of HIV status and treatment. The Middle East and North Africa saw a 78% rise in HIV infections from 2010 to 2025; Latin America about 25%; Eastern Europe and Central Asia 17%, while Sub-Saharan Africa declined. Over 41 million people live with HIV, and 32.1 million are treated (78% coverage). New infections last year totaled 1.2 million, with deaths near 570,000. About 8.9 million people remain untreated, including 5 million unaware of their infection; HIV testing dropped by 13 million tests from 2024 to 2025. Last year saw the decline in official development assistance for HIV (23%), with funding down 18%, creating a financing gap of $4.3 billion. Recommendations call for debt relief, sustainable financing transitions, IP reform for affordable pricing and manufacturing, and integrated, stigma-free services in primary care, TB and chronic disease programs led by affected communities.

triage.headline_ja: UNAIDS報告：ミナ（中東・北アフリカ）地域でHIV感染が78%増加

triage.notes: 「Mina」はアラビア語で中東・北アフリカ（MENA）地域を指す略称であり、フィリピンのMina市やサウジアラビアのMina地区とは無関係。Bluedotの地域付与は誤りと判断。記事はUNAIDSの年次統計報告であり、特定国の急性アウトブレイクイベントではないためDISMISSと判定。

article.articleHeadline: Frutal confirma primeira morte por Covid-19 em 2026; idoso estava sem vacina há quatro anos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Frutal confirms first COVID-19 death in 2026; an elderly man had not been vaccinated for four years.
article.articleSummary: Frutal, in the Triângulo Mineiro region of Minas Gerais, Brazil, reports its first COVID-19 death in 2026. The victim was a 63-year-old man with severe comorbidities, including cancer, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease, who had not updated his vaccination since 2022. He initially presented at Hospital Frei Gabriel in Frutal and was transferred to Uberaba, where he died. The weekly COVID-19 epidemiological bulletin for 13–19 November records three new notifications, three positive cases, and one death. With this death, Frutal totals 46 COVID-19 cases in 2026 and one death this year. Health authorities emphasize vaccination, especially for the elderly and chronically ill; residents should visit the nearest Basic Health Unit with vaccination cards, and if symptomatic, wear a mask and practice hand hygiene to prevent transmission.

article.articleSummary: Uganda launched Africa's first clinical trial of an mRNA Ebola vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain. The study, led by the Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI) in partnership with Moderna, will assess safety and immunogenicity in 224 volunteers, including children aged one year and older. The Bundibugyo strain has driven a major Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo, described as the second-largest globally. article.articleHeadline: Nova variante da Covid-19 circula no ES; veja sintomas e qual é o risco
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New COVID-19 variant circulating in Espírito Santo; see the symptoms and what the risk is.
article.articleSummary: New COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 circulating in Brazil under WHO monitoring as of 2026-11-27; identified in six states including Espírito Santo and the Federal District, with predominance in Rio de Janeiro samples. The WHO classifies PJ.2.1 as a Variant Under Monitoring (VUM), indicating surveillance of its evolution and spread but no evidence of greater virulence or need to change protection measures. PJ.2.1 is a SARS-CoV-2 sublineage derived from Omicron; mutations may facilitate binding to the ACE2 receptor. First detected in Canada in May 2026, it began appearing in Brazil in August 2026 and is now reported in multiple states including Espírito Santo. Common symptoms align with other lineages: fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, fatigue, body aches, and headache; severity varies with age, comorbidity, and vaccination status.

triage.headline_ja: 新型コロナウイルスの新変異株がエスピリトサント州で確認；症状とリスクについて

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19 avança em 23 estados e no DF; Veja quem deve tomar a vacina
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 advances in 23 states and in the Federal District; See who should get the vaccine.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 advances in Brazil: after six weeks of rising infections, the federal government launched WhatsApp and GOV.BR outreach to prompt high‑risk groups to seek care. Over 2.1 million extra doses were distributed to states in 2026, with about 8.5 million already administered (roughly one third of distributed). Severe COVID-19 cases are increasing in 9 jurisdictions—Bahia, Distrito Federal, Espírito Santo, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, and São Paulo—but reported severe incidence remains low. By November 21, 2026, 159,275 notices of COVID-19‑like syndrome were recorded; public RT‑PCR positivity rose from 1.5% to 2.51% in one week, with private labs trending upward for 11 weeks. There were 4,101 SARS‑CoV‑2–related SRAG cases and 481 deaths, predominantly among those 65+, who represented about 68%. PJ.2.1 lineage is expanding in the Southeast (Rio de Janeiro samples 58% of 167, Oct 17–Nov 6); nationwide ~5% of sequences, XFG descendants ~76%. The evidence linking PJ.2.1 to severity is inconclusive; waning immunity may fuel waves. Vaccination guidance remains age/condition‑based, with free doses at UBS and varied intervals; adults 5–59 without priority groups may receive a dose if never vaccinated. Vaccination history can be checked in Meu SUS Digital.

article.articleHeadline: Nova variante da Covid-19 circula no Espírito Santo, aponta Fiocruz
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New COVID-19 variant circulating in Espírito Santo, according to Fiocruz.
article.articleSummary: Espírito Santo, Brazil, reports circulation of SARS-CoV-2 lineage PJ.2.1, a WHO 'variant under monitoring', identified by Fiocruz InfoGripe through sequencing on GISAid. The variant is present in Espírito Santo and in other states (Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul, Mato Grosso) and the Federal District. From Nov 1–26, Espírito Santo registered 5,410 confirmed COVID-19 cases, 7,400 notifications, 6,604 tests, and 1 death; 1,523 cases were under investigation. Vitória led November diagnoses (524), followed by Vila Velha (420) and Serra (386). Fiocruz notes potential higher transmissibility but insufficient genomic data to link PJ.2.1 to increased hospitalizations; vaccines remain protective against severe disease, and SARI linked to COVID-19 is still low in Espírito Santo compared with Rio de Janeiro and Pará. Nationally, SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 22% of SARI positives and 40.6% of related deaths in the last four weeks.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル・エスピリトサント州で新型コロナウイルスの新変異株が流行、フィオクルスが指摘

article.articleHeadline: Aumento dos casos de Covid-19 reforça sistema preventivo em Itaperuna | Itaperuna | O Dia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Increase in COVID-19 cases strengthens the preventive system in Itaperuna | Itaperuna | O Dia
article.articleSummary: Six new COVID-19 cases were confirmed in Itaperuna, in Rio de Janeiro’s Noroeste Fluminense region, last week, prompting renewed vaccination efforts with coverage around 83%. The Municipal Health Secretariat urges residents to update vaccination schedules, especially children, adolescents, the elderly, and other high-risk groups. COVID-19 can range from mild symptoms (fever, cough, sore throat, fatigue, body pains) to severe respiratory disease, hospitalization, sequelae, or death; vaccination remains the main strategy to reduce hospitalizations and deaths. Vaccination services were temporarily relocated from Boa Fortuna UBS to UBS Centro-Vinhosa due to construction; Crie provides pediatric vaccines for 5–11 years, requiring ID, CPF or SUS card, and the vaccination card. Symptomatic individuals should seek medical care. The council also offers vaccines for influenza, measles, polio, yellow fever, hepatitis, HPV, meningitis, tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis, rubella, and others per age. The six cases do not indicate a regional outbreak, but regional vigilance continues.

triage.headline_ja: イタペルナでCOVID-19症例増加、予防体制を強化

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية تصدر توصيات محدثة بشأن الاستجابة لوباء إيبولا.. من سلالة بونديبوجيو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization issues updated recommendations on the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization updates recommendations on Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The emergency committee under the International Health Regulations (2005) issued guidance on 25 November 2026, following the 17 November meeting, confirming the outbreak remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Updates call for accelerated clinical trials of candidate vaccines and therapeutics while upholding rigorous scientific, ethical, and safety standards; emphasize engaging local communities to ensure transparent planning and implementation of trials. As of 24 November, WHO records more than 12,000 Ebola cases and about 5,900 deaths in the DRC. Ongoing insecurity continues to impede response, affecting aid delivery, patients, health workers, and facilities, with at least 94 attacks on health-care facilities since the outbreak was declared a PHEIC six months ago. For non-DRC countries, targeted traveler screening is advised to limit cross-border spread.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Varginha Health Department reinforces dengue, COVID-19, scabies, and tuberculosis prevention and announces D-Day on Saturday (28).
article.articleSummary: Varginha, Minas Gerais, Brazil, reinforces prevention of dengue, COVID-19, scabies, and tuberculosis and announces a dengue D-Day on Saturday, 28 November, at Praça dos Estudantes, Avenida Manoel Vida. Dengue in Minas Gerais totals 50,083 confirmed cases and 54 deaths (Jan–Nov 2026), with a potential epidemic in 2027 and a peak estimated February–March; vaccination for 10–14-year-olds is available across 853 municipalities. In Varginha, there were 229 COVID-19–related ILI cases through 25 November 2026; 10,681 vaccine doses had been administered locally. SRAG notifications reached 324 in 2026 with 26 deaths; 4 SRAG cases were attributed to COVID-19, and no COVID-19 SRAG deaths by 25 November. Scabies outbreaks occurred in about 40 municipalities in Central, Central-West, and Southern Minas. Tuberculosis remains airborne; six months of free SUS treatment; BCG protects young children; emphasize ventilation, hand hygiene, cough etiquette, and early symptom recognition. Seek nearest UBS at first symptom and urgent care if needed.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Severe COVID-19 cases fall 67% in Bahia in 2026, according to a bulletin.
article.articleSummary: Bahia, Brazil, recorded a 67.2% drop in severe COVID-19 cases in 2026 versus the same period in 2025, with COVID-19 deaths down 81.6%, according to Epidemiological Bulletin No. 46 by Sesab, consolidating Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) notifications through epidemiological week 46. The broader SARI burden declined 21.1% in cases and 40.5% in deaths; influenza cases fell 29.4% and deaths 70%. Over half of 2026 SARI cases are attributed to other respiratory viruses, led by rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus. Bahia appears as low-incidence in Fiocruz InfoGripe. Weeks 42-46 saw Salvador and Juazeiro accounting for over 75% of reported severe COVID-19 cases in the state, with few municipalities (<3%). The vaccine, available via SUS, protects against hospitalizations and deaths. Surveillance emphasizes vaccination for children, pregnant women, and the elderly.

article.articleHeadline: Cardiovascular Failure, Hemorrhage, and Age Predict Mortality in Infected
article.articleSummary: From 2015–2023 at a Chinese tertiary center, 5,491 acute pancreatitis patients were studied; 163 with culture-positive infected pancreatic necrosis showed 22.7% mortality. Median age 53 years, 67.5% male; biliary disease 55.8% and hypertriglyceridemia 25.8%; 84.7% had severe acute pancreatitis and 91.4% required ICU care. Microbiology: Gram-negative organisms dominated (70%), led by Klebsiella pneumoniae (28%), with Enterococcus faecium (14%), Acinetobacter baumannii (12.1%), Escherichia coli (10.1%). Multidrug-resistant pathogens were detected in 77.3%, carbapenem resistance 54% overall (62.9% of Gram-negatives). Tigecycline resistance was 0%, but susceptibility testing was incomplete (56.6% G-, 77.6% G+). Cardiovascular failure (OR 18.19), hemorrhage (OR 5.01), and age (OR 1.58 per decade) independently predicted death; CRP ≥125 mg/L was not significant. Internal validation showed AUC ~0.91; external validation required. Empirical antibiotics should align with local resistance patterns.

article.articleHeadline: Scientists Report Strong Evidence That Specially Bred Mosquitoes Can Fend Off Dengue
article.articleSummary: Brazilian Belo Horizonte study of more than 5,700 children over four years shows releasing Wolbachia-carrying Aedes aegypti reduces dengue and chikungunya infections by about 69% in treated neighborhoods versus controls, confirmed by blood tests for dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia are released (males and females); Wolbachia spreads to offspring, rendering local mosquitoes less capable of transmitting viruses. Effect persisted during Brazil's severe 2024 dengue outbreak; findings presented at the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. The World Mosquito Program has pioneered this approach in Indonesia and elsewhere. Separately, as of 2026-11-27, Florida reported an unusually large dengue outbreak with over 650 locally acquired cases, about 75% in Hillsborough County (Tampa).

article.articleHeadline: Actualité | Ebola au Nord-Kivu : le gouverneur suspend les deuils et autorise seulement 20 personnes à participer aux enterrements | mediacongo.net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: News | Ebola in North Kivu: the governor suspends mourning and only 20 people are allowed to participate in the funerals | mediacongo.net.
article.articleSummary: As of 27 November 2026, Ebola cases persist in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with Ituri still the outbreak epicenter. Military Governor General-Major Évariste Somo Kakule announced restrictions suspending mourning rituals, wakes, and religious services across all Ebola-affected health zones, restricting funerals to a maximum of 20 family members. The measures, disclosed by Prisca Luanda Kamala, health coordination lead for the governor, require dignified, secure funerals while enforcing strict barrier precautions. Response teams will manage confirmed cases through decontamination, contact tracing, and isolation of those exposed, with support from relevant services. The governor calls on the response coordination, local and religious authorities, and security services to enforce these measures to curb transmission in affected areas. The steps reflect heightened precautions as North Kivu experiences new cases amid the Ituri outbreak focus.

article.articleHeadline: Mudanças no uso da terra são gatilhos para novas doenças, alerta pesquisadora da Fiocruz Amazônia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Changes in land use are triggers for new diseases, warns a Fiocruz Amazônia researcher.
article.articleSummary: Deforestation and rapid land-use changes in the Amazon, as discussed in the fifth episode of Ciencia em Movimento featuring Alessandra Nava of ILMD/Fiocruz Amazônia, are linked to the emergence of new diseases. The podcast, a collaboration between TV Encontro das Águas and Fapeam (Amazonas Research Foundation), examines how forest loss, unplanned urban growth, and habitat disruption alter human–wildlife interactions, expanding opportunities for pathogen emergence in a biodiversity-rich region. While there is no evidence of immediate human-to-human or vector transmission from these changes, land-use shifts are described as triggers for emerging diseases. The discussion highlights the One Health approach and emphasizes local scientific research, supported by the Amazonas government via Fapeam, for epidemiological surveillance, early risk identification, and public policy to address health threats in the Amazon. The program is available on YouTube.

article.articleHeadline: Canada Extends Visa Curbs Despite End of Uganda's Ebola Outbreak
article.articleSummary: On 2026-11-27, Canada extended Ebola-related visa restrictions through February 25, 2027 for applicants outside Canada who listed Uganda, South Sudan, or the Democratic Republic of Congo as residence. The 90-day extension covers visas, permits and electronic travel authorisations, including those already approved, with applications not to be finalized while measures are in place. Ottawa called the move precautionary to prevent Ebola from entering Canada and will continue monitoring outbreaks in DRC, Uganda and South Sudan. WHO and Africa CDC welcomed the end of Uganda's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak on August 27 after 42 days without a new confirmed case; the last patient, an imported infection, was discharged July 16. Separate border rules require a 21-day quarantine for travelers who visited any of the three countries in the 21 days before arrival, unless exempt.

article.articleHeadline: Passos torna frequência facultativa nas escolas municipais de 30 de novembro a 2 de dezembro por alerta de escabiose
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Passos makes attendance optional in municipal schools from November 30 to December 2 due to a scabies alert.
article.articleSummary: Passos, Minas Gerais, Brazil, announced municipal school attendance will be voluntary from November 30 to December 2, 2026, with normal activities resuming December 3. The measure aims to reduce human scabies transmission in schools and facilitate care for symptomatic children. Scabies is caused by a skin mite; it is not life-threatening but causes intense itching and small skin lesions; incubation is four to six weeks. Transmission occurs mainly through prolonged skin contact, with schools and day-care centers at higher risk. Minas Gerais reports outbreaks in 40 municipalities across the Central, Central-West, and South regions in 2026. Prevention includes avoiding sharing clothes, towels, and bed linens; washing fabrics at 55-60°C for 20 minutes, then ironing or dryer; sealing non-washable items for 72 hours; cleaning objects with soap and water. Seek guidance at a Basic Health Unit for oral and topical treatment; contacts may require treatment even if asymptomatic.

article.articleHeadline: 中國疫情急速上升 心梗患者不分年齡大小 | 新冠疫情 | 新冠口服藥 | 新冠病毒
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 outbreak is rapidly accelerating | Myocardial Infarction Patients Across All Age Groups | COVID-19 Pandemic | COVID-19 Oral Antiviral Drugs | SARS-CoV-2
article.articleSummary: China’s COVID-19 outbreak is rapidly accelerating as authorities allow pharmacies to sell oral antiviral drugs, though stock remains limited. Health officials warn that influenza and SARS-CoV-2 infections can trigger cytokine storms and provoke four cardiovascular conditions—myocarditis; coronary events (angina or myocardial infarction); arrhythmias; and pericarditis—leading to severe illness across age groups. Hospitals report overwhelmed facilities and widespread inflammation, with Guangdong’s ICU capacity fully strained and many pediatric patients among the critically ill. Personal accounts describe a Guangdong 37-year-old man who rapidly worsened from fever to coma and remained in ICU for more than 50 days amid multi-organ inflammation, including encephalitis; a 3-year-old survivor who suffered a blockage and later became diabetic; and a Henan resident, a 31-year-old man, who survived an acute myocardial infarction after prompt rescue. Authorities have not released comprehensive nationwide data.

article.articleHeadline: Nova variante pode estar relacionada ao aumento de casos de covid-19 no Brasil
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New variant may be linked to the rise in COVID-19 cases in Brazil.
article.articleSummary: Eight Brazilian states and the Federal District show rising severe COVID-19-associated SARI cases, with a shift potentially linked to the PJ.2.1 variant. Fiocruz's Infogripe bulletin reports increases in Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Espírito Santo, Paraná, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul, Bahia, and the Distrito Federal, though overall SARI incidence remains low. Mato Grosso shows oscillations; Pará and Rio de Janeiro are at alert levels, as are the capitals Porto Velho and Rio Branco. Data cover 15–21 November; Brasília and Cuiabá also at alert/risk but without long-term growth. In Rio de Janeiro, SARI is also linked to metapneumovirus and influenza A and B. The PJ.2.1 variant is under OMS surveillance since 19 November; booster-dose coverage decline may increase cases. No current evidence of reduced vaccine protection against PJ.2.1; vaccines remain primary protection.

triage.headline_ja: 新変異株がブラジルにおける新型コロナウイルス感染症症例増加に関連している可能性

triage.notes: 新変異株PJ.2.1は2026年11月19日からWHOの監視下にあり、ブラジル複数州で重症SARI症例の増加が報告されている。全体のSARI発生率は依然低いが、ブースター接種率低下による症例増加の可能性が指摘されている。現時点でワクチン防御力低下の証拠はない。

article.articleHeadline: கடலூரில் பறவைக் காய்ச்சல் எதிரொலி: நாமக்கல் கோழிப் பண்ணைகளைக் கண்காணிக்க 45 குழுக்கள் அமைப்பு
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Cuddalore, avian influenza aftermath: 45 teams formed to monitor Namakkal poultry farms.
article.articleSummary: As of 27 November 2026, following avian influenza in Cuddalore district, authorities culled more than 50,000 chickens there. In the Namakkal division, 45 special teams have been constituted to monitor poultry farms. Namakkal houses over 1,000 poultry farms and around 80 million layer chickens, producing roughly 70 million eggs daily, which supply Tamil Nadu’s public food security scheme and are exported domestically and to other states; trucks transport eggs to various districts. In response to the Cuddalore outbreak, biosecurity measures have been tightened in Namakkal farms, with vehicles disinfected prior to entry. The Namakkal district animal husbandry department-constituted teams are conducting intensified farm inspections to verify compliance with biosafety protocols. According to Selvakumar, joint director, mortality in Cuddalore is currently low, and Namakkal teams continue routine surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: മലേറിയ: കളി ഇനി കാലാവസ്ഥയോട്
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria: The game now with the weather.
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a major target for India’s public health. From 2015 to 2025, cases and deaths fell by about 80%. District reporting declined from 155 to 33, and between 2022 and 2025 roughly 160 districts had no reported cases. Despite progress, experts warn against complacency as climate change and shifting rainfall threaten gains. Plasmodium parasites are transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes; rising temperatures, irregular rainfall, and changing seasons alter vector breeding and may expand reach to new areas and higher elevations. Symptoms typically appear 10–15 days after the bite and include fever with chills, sweating, severe headache, muscle pains, fatigue, vomiting, and dizziness. Diagnosis uses blood-smear microscopy or rapid tests; treatment depends on parasite type and illness severity. Prevention focuses on avoiding bites, bed nets, repellents, covering clothing, and eliminating standing water. India aims for malaria elimination by 2030, requiring sustained surveillance and public-health measures against climate-driven challenges.

triage.headline_ja: マラリア：気候変動との新たな闘い
triage.triage_reason: インドのマラリア症例・死亡数は過去10年で80%減少しており、本記事は気候変動による将来的リスクへの注意喚起であり、現時点で異常な増加や緊急の公衆衛生事案は報告されていない。
triage.notes: 本記事はマラリア減少傾向と気候変動による将来リスクに関する啓発的内容であり、急性のアウトブレイク情報ではないため対象国としての報告は不要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Sorocaba registra índice de risco para dengue em outubro; região tem maior concentração de larvas | TVS+
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sorocaba records dengue risk index in October; the region has the highest concentration of larvae | TVS+
article.articleSummary: Sorocaba recorded October larval-density index (Aedes aegypti) of 4.9, placing the city at dengue transmission risk. The northwest region is the most worrisome at 9.82, including São Bento, São Guilherme, Maria Eugênia and Vila Barão. The southwest and north regions register elevated indices of 6.17 (Júlio de Mesquita, Wanel Ville, Jardim Simus, Cerrado) and 4.31 (Laranjeiras, Paineiras, Vitória Régia, Conjunto Habitacional Ana Paula Eleutério). Sorocaba has 106 confirmed dengue cases in 2026, with 21 showing warning signs; 11 are under investigation and no deaths yet. Zoonoses will inspect suspected breeding sites on Saturday. In São Paulo state, the Day D dengue prevention accompanies a statewide total of 65,671 confirmed cases and 45 deaths for 2026; residents are urged to remove standing water, wash animal water bowls, clean gutters, and seal water tanks.

triage.headline_ja: ソロカバ、10月にデング熱リスク指数を記録；地域で幼虫密度が最も高い | TVS+
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・サンパウロ州で通常のデング熱流行期の監視情報であり、重症度や国際的拡大の兆候は見られないが、州全体での症例数・死亡者数が一定規模あるため継続監視が妥当。
triage.notes: ソロカバ市および州レベルでの季節性デング熱監視・予防活動の報告。地方自治体（Zoonoses）が通常の対策を実施しており、特段の異常事態ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Nova Friburgo já tem 341 casos confirmados de Covid em 2026 entre residentes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nova Friburgo already has 341 confirmed COVID-19 cases in 2026 among residents.
article.articleSummary: Nova Friburgo, Rio de Janeiro State, reports 341 confirmed COVID-19 cases among residents from January 1 to November 23, 2026, up 152.6% from 135 in 2025. statewide, 2026 totals reach 20,196 confirmed cases, 656 hospitalizations, and 81 deaths through November 27; 2,424 cases occurred in the most recent week (Nov 15–21) with nowcasting estimating 2,614 for that period. Omicron remains dominant; since late August MC.10.1.7 circulated, though PJ.2.1 and RF.5.3 now predominate in samples. Public test positivity rose from 25.9% to 34.3%. Adults with flu‑like symptoms seeking UPAs increased (1,652 to 1,981) and pediatric visits rose (859 to 1,048). Vaccination totaled 721,950 doses in 2026 (to Nov 24); 2025 saw 679,322 doses. Vaccination follows the Ministry of Health/PNI guidelines; data available on SES-RJ Monitora panel.

triage.headline_ja: ノヴァ・フリブルゴ、2026年の住民における新型コロナウイルス確定症例が341件に
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19は既に風土病化しており、本記事はブラジル・リオデジャネイロ州における定例の疫学監視報告であり、新規性・異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: ブラジルは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations は空配列とする。記事内容は地方自治体の定例サーベイランスデータ公表であり、既存変異株（Omicron系統）の範囲内の動向。

article.articleHeadline: Justiça dá cinco dias para governo do RS explicar ações contra esporotricose | abc+
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Court gives five days for the Rio Grande do Sul government to explain measures against sporotrichosis | abc+
article.articleSummary: Sporotrichosis in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, prompts a court-ordered five-day deadline for the state government to detail actions against the disease in animals and humans. Judge Patrícia Antunes Laydner underscored the urgency amid expanding cases and potential laboratory disruption at IPVDF. The civil action by the National Association of Animal Lawyers demands the state report on diagnosis capacity, drug supply (itraconazole and potassium iodide for animals), epidemiological surveillance, and animal protection measures. In 2026, more than 7,000 animal cases were notified, 99% in cats, with Sapucaia do Sul registering 1,446 notifications—the state's highest. Human cases reached 1,465 confirmed in 2026, with 1,051 under investigation; 2025 saw 1,960 infections. Canoas (156 confirmed) leads human cases, followed by Porto Alegre (142) and Alvorada (119). The court requires clarifications on the State Plan, diagnostic network capacity (IPVDF), data, municipal support, animal care structures, budgets, and emergency measures, with a public hearing set for December 11 in Porto Alegre.

triage.headline_ja: リオグランデ・ド・スル州政府に対し、裁判所がスポロトリコーシス対策の説明を5日以内に求める
triage.triage_reason: リオグランデ・ド・スル州でスポロトリコーシス（動物7,000件超、人1,465件確認）が急増し、裁判所が州政府に対策説明を命じるなど、公衆衛生上の影響と異常な拡大傾向が認められるためIHR基準2項目に該当する。
triage.notes: 猫由来の人獣共通感染症として症例数が急増しており、州の診断・治療体制の不備が司法介入の対象となっている。国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候はないが、国内公衆衛生対応力の不足が懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: BH tem Dia D de combate à dengue neste sábado (28/11)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Belo Horizonte to hold D-Day to combat dengue this Saturday (Nov 28).
article.articleSummary: Belo Horizonte, Brazil reports 1,991 dengue cases among residents in 2026, with 1,323 awaiting results (3,314 probable) and 17,238 discarded; four dengue deaths. Chikungunya totals rise to 82 cases with no deaths (35 local, 6 imported, 41 with unknown origin; 13 pending). Zika has two cases notified and discarded. On 28 November 2026, the city launches a D-Day against Aedes aegypti, intensifying inspections of about 53,000 properties; 2.4% had larvae (LIRAa 2026) and 83% of breeding sites are in residences. Main habitats: plant saucers 24.7%, discarded materials 23.2%, domestic containers 17.7%, barrels 7.2%. Dengue hotspots by region are Nordeste (589 probable; 485 confirmed, 104 suspected) and Venda Nova (562; 399 confirmed, 163 suspected). The campaign includes home visits, larviciding when needed, and community education; over 3.5 million actions have been conducted to date.

triage.headline_ja: ベロオリゾンテ、今週土曜(11/28)にデング熱対策の「D-Day」を実施
triage.triage_reason: 通常の季節性デング熱対策活動であり、公的な蚊対策キャンペーンの報告に過ぎず、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 地方自治体による定例的な蚊対策（LIRAa調査・D-Dayキャンペーン）の報告であり、デング熱・チクングニア熱は例年発生している流行病のため、特段のシグナルとして扱う必要はない。

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19 sobe em 21 estados, e Ministério reforça vacinação por WhatsApp | Prensa Mercosur
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 cases rise in 21 states, and the Ministry reinforces vaccination via WhatsApp
article.articleSummary: As of 27 November 2026, COVID-19 cases rise in 21 Brazilian states, with Rio de Janeiro at SRAG alert. The Health Ministry is promoting vaccination via WhatsApp and GOV.BR. Influenza-like illness notifications reached about 135,000 in 2026 through mid-November. Since November, XFG accounts for about 90% of cases nationwide; the vaccines cover this variant. A November 17 death in Governador Valadares involved a 70–79-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes who was unvaccinated. For 2026, COVID-19 deaths fell 68% to 468; SRAG hospitalizations down 54% to ~3,900. Vaccination: 25.7M doses distributed, 8.5M administered; 2.1M extra doses; over 3M rapid tests (1.9M extra). People with permanent disabilities join the special vaccination groups with an annual dose; symptomatic testing and wearing PFF2/N95 masks indoors are advised.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19が21州で増加、保健省がWhatsAppでワクチン接種を強化
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19・インフルエンザの季節的な増加に伴う通常の公衆衛生対応であり、死亡・入院数は前年比で大幅減少しているため、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 死亡数（468人、前年比68%減）、SRAG入院数（約3900件、54%減）と改善傾向にあり、ワクチン接種キャンペーンの一環としての通常の季節性報道と判断。XFG株が優勢だが既存ワクチンでカバーされている。

article.articleHeadline: В Санкт-Петербурге выявили третий за сутки случай заражения оспой обезьян
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Saint Petersburg, the third case of monkeypox infection in 24 hours was detected.
article.articleSummary: As of 27 November 2026, Saint Petersburg reports the third monkeypox case in 24 hours. The patient returned from a trip to Thailand; two previously hospitalized with suspected monkeypox also had recent travel from Thailand and are in satisfactory condition. The Interregional Office of Rospotrebnadzor for Saint Petersburg and Leningrad Oblast has launched a sanitary-epidemiological investigation. Monkeypox causes fever, intoxication, lymphadenopathy, and a subsequent skin rash; uncomplicated cases typically recover without specific treatment in about two to three weeks. Mortality ranges from 0.1% to 11%, depending on the viral strain and the patient’s health. All three cases are linked to importation from Thailand, highlighting ongoing surveillance of imported infections.

triage.headline_ja: サンクトペテルブルクで24時間以内に3例目の猿痘（mpox）感染が確認される
triage.triage_reason: ロシア（対象国外）で24時間以内に3例のmpox感染が報告され、いずれもタイからの渡航者に関連しているが、タイ国内での発生を示す情報はなく、重症度も低いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 発生地域はロシア（サンクトペテルブルク）であり対象国リストに含まれない。タイは患者の渡航元として言及されているのみで、タイ国内での発生・流行を示す記述はないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Роспотребнадзор раскрыл, откуда оспа обезьян попала в российский город
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rospotrebnadzor revealed where monkeypox arrived in a Russian city.
article.articleSummary: Third monkeypox case reported in Saint Petersburg within 24 hours, involving a resident who had returned from a tourist trip; two earlier cases were travelers from Thailand. All recently diagnosed patients were hospitalized; doctors describe their condition as stable. Authorities have organized full anti-epidemic measures and are tracing contacts who may have been exposed. Rospotrebnadzor launched a sanitary-epidemiological investigation and ordered disinfection in affected facilities. Earlier, two people were brought to hospital with suspected monkeypox; they were reportedly treated at Botkinskaya Hospital. The events indicate travel-associated monkeypox cases in Saint Petersburg, with ongoing monitoring of transmission and exposure risk as of 2026-11-27.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア消費者保護監督庁、サンクトペテルブルクへのサル痘侵入経路を公表
triage.triage_reason: 発生国はロシアであり、対象監視国（タイ等）は渡航元として言及されているのみで実際の発生地ではないため、対象国に該当する事案ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はロシア・サンクトペテルブルクでの渡航関連サル痘症例（タイからの帰国者含む）を報告。対象監視国リストに含まれる国での発生ではないため、本トリアージでは対象外と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Uganda launches trial of mRNA Ebola vaccine
article.articleSummary: Uganda on 2026-11-27 launched clinical trials of a Moderna mRNA Ebola vaccine to address the Bundibugyo strain behind the deadly outbreak in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. The trials test this mRNA vaccine alongside another candidate vaccine. The effort aims to find a treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola; no case counts, fatalities, or laboratory-confirmation details are provided. The Bundibugyo strain is a member of the Ebola virus species linked to outbreaks near Uganda, and the work underscores regional attempts to advance vaccination options in response to the DRC outbreak. As of 2026-11-27, timelines, enrollment figures, and results are not disclosed in the report.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ、mRNA型エボラワクチンの治験を開始
triage.triage_reason: 隣国DRCで進行中のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）アウトブレイクに対するワクチン治験開始であり、エボラの重篤性と国際的拡大リスクからIHR基準を2つ満たすためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダでのワクチン治験開始が主題だが、根本の感染症イベントはDRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）アウトブレイク。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを記載。症例数・死亡者数・治験登録数などの詳細は記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Casos graves de covid-19 oscilam em Mato Grosso e Cuiabá registra nível de alerta
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Severe COVID-19 cases fluctuate in Mato Grosso, and Cuiabá records an alert level.
article.articleSummary: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) cases linked to COVID-19 oscillate in Mato Grosso, Brazil. In Cuiabá, COVID-19 incidence is at alert/high-risk but shows no clear long-term upward trend; data refer to Nov 15–21. Nationally, the rise may be linked to circulation of the PJ.2.1 variant, possibly more transmissible, and waning population immunity. Preliminary data do not indicate loss of vaccine protection against the new variant. Fiocruz Infogripe stresses vaccination as the main prevention against severe COVID-19 and ongoing immunization campaigns. No specific case counts or lab confirmation details are provided; monitoring continues, with Cuiabá's alert status highlighting regional risk without sustained growth.

triage.headline_ja: マトグロッソ州で新型コロナウイルス重症例が増減、クイアバ市は警戒レベルを記録
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の新変異株(PJ.2.1)の流行が報告されているが、地域限定的なモニタリング情報であり、重症度や拡大の明確な上昇傾向は確認されていないため継続注視が妥当。
triage.notes: 新変異株PJ.2.1の国内（ブラジル）流行についての言及があるが、具体的な症例数・重症度データは不足。ワクチン効果の低下は確認されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Alza de Covid-19 en Brasil asociada posiblemnte a nueva variante
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rise in COVID-19 cases in Brazil possibly linked to a new variant.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Brazil shows rising Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS-CoV-2) activity, with Covid-19–associated SRAG increasing, though national levels remain low, per Fiocruz InfoGripe. The uptick is observed in Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Espírito Santo, Paraná, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul, Bahia, and the Distrito Federal; Mato Grosso reports oscillations in severe cases, while Pará and Rio de Janeiro are at SRAG incidence alert. The capitals of Rondônia and Acre also show a similar rise. The period analyzed covers November 15–21. The increase may be linked to the SARS-CoV-2 variant PJ.2.1, under WHO surveillance since November 19 and detected across DF, Espírito Santo, São Paulo, Mato Grosso, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul, and Santa Catarina. Waning immunity due to lower recent booster uptake is noted; authorities urge up-to-date vaccination—especially for older adults and immunocompromised—and sustained epidemiological and genomic surveillance to guide responses.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルにおける新型コロナウイルス感染症の増加、新変異株との関連の可能性
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル国内でCOVID-19関連SRAGの増加と新変異株（PJ.2.1）の検出が報告されているが、全国レベルでは依然として低水準であり、現時点で重大な公衆衛生インパクトは確認されていないため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: WHOが監視中の新変異株PJ.2.1がブラジル複数州で検出されており、免疫低下（ブースター接種率低下）も指摘されている。全国的な数値は低いが、複数州で重症例の増加傾向が見られるため今後の動向を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Tia Nastácia do 'Sítio do Picapau Amarelo', atriz é internada com leishmaniose
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Aunt Nastácia from 'Sítio do Picapau Amarelo,' actress hospitalized with leishmaniasis.
article.articleSummary: Rosa Marya Colin, 81, the actress who portrayed Aunt Nastácia in the 2007 Rede Globo adaptation of Sítio do Picapau Amarelo, is hospitalized in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil after being diagnosed with leishmaniasis. She was admitted to Hospital Universitário de Campo Grande on November 23, 2026. The actress and singer is receiving medication and her condition is stable, according to g1. The report provides no details on laboratory confirmation, the specific form of leishmaniasis, or other affected individuals. She remains under medical care, with no additional clinical details disclosed in the article. The update does not include travel history, exposure details, or prognosis.

triage.headline_ja: 『シチオ・ド・ピカパウ・アマレロ』のチア・ナスタシア役、女優がリーシュマニア症で入院
triage.triage_reason: 単一著名人の個別症例報告であり、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や異常性、国際的拡大のリスクを示す情報がない。
triage.notes: リーシュマニア症はブラジルの一部地域で流行があるが、本記事は著名人の個別症例のみを扱い、集団発生やアウトブレイクを示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Após surto de sarna humana e covid-19, cidade de MG cancela parte de programação de Natal
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: After outbreak of human scabies and COVID-19, a city in Minas Gerais cancels part of Christmas programming.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 and human scabies outbreaks in Divinópolis, Central-West Minas Gerais, prompted a health emergency declaration on 26 November 2026 and the cancellation of cultural/festive attractions for the Christmas light ceremonies on 28–29 November, while the Christmas Illumination event remains with crowd-control guidance. As of 26 November, Divinópolis reported 316 confirmed COVID-19 cases and 104 scabies cases in November (91 in children across 19 schools; 13 adults). The emergency protocol includes identifying suspected cases, removing infected students from school, environmental cleaning, and potential school suspensions if three positives occur in a single day. Infected students must remain out of school for 48 hours after starting treatment; symptomatic unassessed students cannot attend until health teams advise differently. Authorities will expand awareness campaigns with Health and Education Secretaries. Minas Gerais SES notes no epidemiological pattern shift, though 43 municipalities report scabies outbreaks statewide.

triage.headline_ja: 疥癬とCOVID-19の集団発生後、ミナスジェライス州の都市がクリスマスプログラムの一部を中止
triage.triage_reason: ミナスジェライス州の一都市で疥癬とCOVID-19の集団発生により健康緊急事態が宣言されたが、州当局は疫学的パターンの変化はないとしており、重症度・国際的拡大リスクは低い。地域限定的な事案として続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 疥癬104例（うち学童91例、19校）とCOVID-19確定316例が報告され、学校での感染拡大防止策（隔離・環境清掃・休校措置）が実施されている。州全体で43自治体が疥癬アウトブレイクを報告しているが、州保健当局は疫学パターンの変化はないとしている。国際的な影響は限定的と判断。

article.articleHeadline: أوغندا تبدأ اختبار لقاح تجريبي مضاد لإيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Uganda begins trial of an experimental Ebola vaccine
article.articleSummary: Uganda begins a trial of an experimental Ebola vaccine, announced by the Uganda Virus Research Institute, as part of the response to the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak that has caused about 5,700 deaths among roughly 11,000 cases since May, with most fatalities in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Uganda has reported around 20 infections and 2 deaths, and the outbreak there was declared over in August. The Ugandan trial tests a Moderna-developed messenger RNA vaccine, described by the institute as Africa’s first Phase I trial of an mRNA Ebola vaccine, enrolling 224 healthy volunteers aged 1–65 to assess immune response. In DR Congo, trials begin for a second vaccine developed by Serum Institute of India and University of Oxford, based on the ChAdOx1 viral-vector platform, targeting close contacts and high-risk groups. Gavi has signed a deal to purchase 1.5 million doses. The trials are hoped to yield results in early 2027.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ、エボラ治験ワクチンの試験を開始
triage.triage_reason: DRCを中心に約11,000例・5,700人死亡という極めて深刻なエボラアウトブレイクが継続しており、国際機関（Gavi、Moderna、Oxford/Serum Institute）が関与する大規模対応が進行中であるため、フルリスク評価の対象とすべき。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はワクチン治験開始だが、背景情報としてBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる大規模アウトブレイク（DRC中心、約11,000例・5,700死亡）が継続中であることが述べられている。ウガンダでの感染は8月に終息宣言済みで対象国リストにも含まれないため、verified_locationsからは除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Actualité | La poliomyélite, la rougeole et la rubéole au Kasaï Oriental : après 67 morts, Mbwebwa Kapo lance une double vaccination | mediacongo.net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: News | Polio, measles and rubella in Kasai-Oriental: after 67 deaths, Mbwebwa Kapo launches a double vaccination | mediacongo.net
article.articleSummary: Kasai-Oriental, Democratic Republic of the Congo, reports 4,687 measles cases and 67 deaths in 2026, prompting a double vaccination campaign against polio, measles, and rubella. Governor Jean-Paul Mbwebwa Kapo launched the initiative at Mbuji-Mayi’s University roundabout on November 27, 2026. The polio vaccination runs November 28–30 and targets 1,254,297 children aged 0–59 months province-wide. The measles and rubella vaccination aims to reach 2,927,905 children aged 6–14 years. Authorities, backed by the central government, WHO and UNICEF, emphasize vaccination as the safest protection against these diseases and urge parents to participate. The campaign seeks to boost immunization coverage and eradicate vaccine-preventable illnesses in Kasai-Oriental amid the ongoing measles burden and related deaths.

triage.headline_ja: ニュース | 東カサイ州でポリオ・麻疹・風疹が流行：67人死亡後、ムブウェブワ・カポ氏が二重ワクチン接種を開始
triage.triage_reason: 東カサイ州で麻疹4,687例・67人死亡という深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、WHO/UNICEFの支援を伴う大規模ワクチンキャンペーンが実施されるなど政府・国際機関の関心が高いため、フルリスク評価に進むべきと判断した。
triage.notes: 麻疹は既往の継続的流行とされ「異常/予想外」には該当しないが、死亡者数とワクチン未接種人口の規模から重症度・拡大可能性が高く、WHO/UNICEF支援下での大規模対応が進行中。
